contracts.text: `Expr` and `Series` namespaces each expose a `rolling_min` method with signature `rolling_min(window_size, *, min_samples=None, center=False)`.
`Expr` and `Series` namespaces each expose a `rolling_max` method with signature `rolling_max(window_size, *, min_samples=None, center=False)`.
`Expr` and `Series` namespaces each expose a `rolling_median` method with signature `rolling_median(window_size, *, min_samples=None, center=False)`.
`Expr` and `Series` namespaces each expose a `rolling_quantile` method with signature `rolling_quantile(window_size, *, quantile, interpolation='linear', min_samples=None, center=False)`.
In `rolling_quantile`, the `quantile` parameter is a required keyword-only argument with no default value.
In `rolling_quantile`, the `interpolation` parameter defaults to the string `'linear'`.
contracts.adverse_condition: when interpolation is not provided by the caller — the default value must be 'linear', not another interpolation method.

contracts.text: When `min_samples` is `None` (or not provided), it defaults to `window_size`.
contracts.adverse_condition: when min_samples is None or omitted — explicit min_samples values bypass the defaulting logic.

contracts.text: When `center=True`, the window is centered around the current observation.
contracts.adverse_condition: when center is True — center=False takes a different code path and cannot verify centering.

contracts.text: Null inputs are excluded from the window.
contracts.adverse_condition: when the window contains null values — all-non-null windows do not exercise null exclusion.

contracts.text: A window with fewer than `min_samples` non-null values produces null.
contracts.adverse_condition: when the number of non-null values in the window is strictly less than min_samples.

contracts.text: For lazy backends (Polars, DuckDB, Dask), the rolling operation must be followed by `.over()` with `order_by` specified.
contracts.adverse_condition: when the backend is lazy (Polars, DuckDB, or Dask) — eager backends do not require .over().

contracts.text: Calling `rolling_quantile` with `quantile` outside [0, 1] raises `ValueError` with a message starting with `"Quantile must be between 0.0 and 1.0"`.
The error message for an out-of-range quantile must start with the exact string `"Quantile must be between 0.0 and 1.0"`.
Calling `rolling_quantile` with `interpolation` not in `{'linear', 'lower', 'higher', 'nearest', 'midpoint'}` raises `ValueError` with a message starting with `"Interpolation must be one of"`.
contracts.adverse_condition: when interpolation is a string not among the five valid values.

contracts.text: The error message for an invalid interpolation must start with the exact string `"Interpolation must be one of"`.
`rolling_quantile` must accept `interpolation` values `'linear'`, `'lower'`, `'higher'`, `'nearest'`, and `'midpoint'` without raising.
DuckDB does not support `rolling_quantile` with `.over()`; the operation is not available on the DuckDB backend.
